observations: The medRxiv API returned two preprint versions dated 10 and 11 September 2020.
The publication-link endpoint associated the preprint with Nature Communications DOI 10.1038/s41467-021-21444-5.
PubMed identifies the linked publication as PMID 33608522, published 19 February 2021.
Rosalind Workbench returned its ready task chooser for the recorded case-specific invocation.
interpretation: The example demonstrates a traceable preprint-to-publication relationship with a changed title and a computed 162-day interval.
limitations: Publication-link services can omit or update relationships.
A linkage indicates record continuity, not equivalence of every claim, analysis, or dataset version.
The Rosalind call opened only the task chooser and did not execute a scientific job.

actual_tools: public literature APIs and local Python
execution.implementation: dated medRxiv, PubMed, and DOI evidence, deterministic local chronology, and a genuine Rosalind task-chooser observation

provenance.note: The preprint and publication APIs produced the chronology; the separate Rosalind observation preserves the genuine task-chooser response and states that no scientific job ran.

reproduction: Run the medRxiv details and publication-link requests for DOI 10.1101/2020.09.09.20191205 and compare outputs/query-verification.json.
Recompute the 162-day interval from the returned preprint and publication dates.
Inspect the preview while keeping API-reported linkage separate from project interpretation of the title change.
Compare any new Rosalind launcher response with outputs/rosalind-open-observation.json without treating it as publication-link evidence.
